hints.title: State the counterexample test
hints.body: You need f′(x)>0 for every real x, but f(x)≤0 for at least one real x.
hints.recap: The derivative condition is universal; the height condition needs one failure.
hints.pitfall: A negative function value alone does not suffice if the derivative premise fails.

recall.reminder: Whole-function counterexamples must satisfy the hypothesis throughout the stated domain.

hints.title: Separate gradient from height
hints.body: Differentiate the polynomial candidates and test the sign of each derivative across the full real domain.
hints.recap: Positive derivative concerns rise, not height above the axis.
hints.pitfall: A positive derivative at one input is insufficient.
hints.pause: Identify candidates with an everywhere-positive derivative.

recall.reminder: Positive derivative concerns rise, not height above the axis.

hints.title: Find a height exception
hints.body: For a candidate meeting the derivative premise, test small negative inputs and check whether the required strict height inequality still holds.
hints.recap: One height failure is enough after the full derivative premise is proved.
hints.pitfall: An exponential’s positive height cannot refute positivity.
hints.pause: Verify both halves of the counterexample condition before selecting the function.

recall.reminder: One height failure is enough after the full derivative premise is proved.

solution:
For C, f(x)=x3+x+1, so f′(x)=3x2+1≥1>0 for every real x. Thus the hypothesis is satisfied globally.

But f(−1)=−1−1+1=−1<0. Hence the conclusion that f(x)>0 for all x is false.

The quadratic options have derivative 2 x, and D has derivative−1, so they fail the premise. E, the exponential 2x, is positive everywhere and does not refute the conclusion.

C is the required counterexample.
knowledgePattern: Choose a function with positive derivative everywhere but some nonpositive values
